text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary deployment v2.3.0 showing elevated 5xx rate (aggregate 7.8%) and latency spike in us-west-2. Triggering paging for #incidents.

amanda_oncall: ack — I'm on it. Paging the release owner and SRE.

rick_platform: i'm the release owner for this deploy. seeing the same in dashboards, canary group has error rate 8.2% over last 2m. Connections failing on /generate endpoint.

jas_sre: joining. first check: are there any recent infra changes? autoscaling events?

deploy-bot: Deploy started by emily_releases at 2024-08-11T21:20:15Z — rollout strategy: canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%), current stage: 5%.

alec_runtime: quick glance at logs: stacktrace originates from cuda kernel timeout in runtime on a small subset of backends. Some requests fall back to a CPU path causing long tail latencies.

maria_product: product reports a handful of customer errors — support ticket #3458 flagged it. Noticed via monitoring.

amanda_oncall: determine blast radius: tom, can you check incoming tickets and if any paying customers are affected?

tom_support: confirming: two enterprise customers reported request timeouts. both on dedicated clusters in us-west-2. Escalating to account success.

rick_platform: hypothesis: canary model binary built with a different runtime ABI; fallback path triggers on certain seq lengths. I'm putting a kill-switch on the feature flag to stop routing traffic to the canary set.

amanda_oncall: good. what's the flag key?

rick_platform: flag key: rollout.enable_v2_3_0. I will toggle to off. Command: ```curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_API' https://flags.redwood.io/toggle -d '{"key":"rollout.enable_v2_3_0","state":false}'```

rick_platform: executed. response: {"ok":true,"old_state":true,"new_state":false}. Setting immediate fallback to stable model variant.

incident-bot: NOTE: Feature flag rollout.enable_v2_3_0 set to false by rick_platform — automatic routing reverted to stable.

jas_sre: monitoring now. within 30s error rate dropped to 1.1% but latency still a bit elevated compared to baseline. Looks like queued requests are draining.

alec_runtime: confirming that KV cache warmed on stable path, but we still have some in-flight requests hitting slow fallback CPU path. If we want to fully revert the canary we should also undo the canary deployment on the cluster to avoid partial routing quirks.

emily_releases: i'm preparing a controlled rollback of the canary Deployment object. Plan: kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-canary --to-revision=3 then scale to 0 for canary replicas temporarily. Any objections?

amanda_oncall: go for it. coordinate so we don't clobber other clusters. Priority: return customer-facing SLA.

emily_releases: running: ```kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-canary --to-revision=3 && kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-canary --replicas=0```

deploy-bot: Rollout undo started. Rolling back ReplicaSet rs-inference-canary-3.

rick_platform: also updating routing policy in the load-splitter to 100% stable for us-west-2 to ensure no residual traffic. Command: `splitctl set --region us-west-2 --stable 100`.

jas_sre: observing backend metrics: error rate at 0.9%, p95 latency back within 10% of baseline. Good.

maria_product: customer impact: two tickets open — told both customers we're rolling back and will follow up. They acknowledged. No major data loss reported.

tom_support: adding notes to tickets and escalating to account teams.

alec_runtime: post-rollback checklist: 1) confirm canary pods are scaled to 0 2) ensure the model artifact v2.3.0 is quarantined in registry 3) capture runtime logs from affected nodes for root cause.

emily_releases: canary pods are 0/0. Confirmed. I've added a tag quarantined=true on the artifact in the model registry.

jas_sre: collected logs from affected instances and uploaded to incident bucket s3://redwood-incidents/1820001234/logs. Zip: 1820001234-runtime-logs.tar.gz.

amanda_oncall: good work. next: verification steps before we close this page: - validate p50/p95/p99 for /generate back to baseline - verify account tickets updated - confirm no automated retry storms queued in job queue - make postmortem owner assignment.

rick_platform: I'll own postmortem and follow-up with a proposed rollback hardening doc.

maria_product: i'll own customer comms follow-up and coordinate with success.

jas_sre: oncall follow-up: i'll run through the incident runbook and make a short checklist for canary ABI compatibility checks to add to predeploy gating.

amanda_oncall: assigning incident severity: Sev2 (partial outage for a subset of customers). Starting incident timeline doc.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Incident status -> mitigated. Time to mitigation: ~4 minutes from first alert.

emily_releases: final verification: p95 within 8% of baseline, error rate <0.5% in last 5m. Holding for another 15m for stability.

tom_support: informed customers that mitigation complete and we're investigating next steps.

alec_runtime: quick notes for RMS: probable cause: runtime ABI mismatch causing GPU kernel path to hit a guard condition leading to fallback CPU behavior and timeouts under certain request shapes. Need stricter build/test gating + canary runtime smoke tests.

rick_platform: noted. I will create a ticket with reproduction steps and label it priority-high.

amanda_oncall: thanks everyone. i'll hand off to the normal post-incident workflow: create incident ticket, add timeline, and schedule postmortem meeting. If anything new pops up, ping this thread. :thumbsup:

maria_product: thanks, team.

emily_releases: thanks.

jas_sre: handshake.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated -> monitoring).
